1. **The idea.** The animation compares buying with renting using US history. It takes every possible start month from January 1991 onward and follows each one for ten years. The data sources are FHFA home prices, BLS rents and Freddie Mac mortgage rates. Each month is a tile in a grid. A lit tile means the buyer was ahead after ten years, and a dark tile means the renter was ahead. Later frames turn the tiles into a field of small houses. The last two frames switch to a single illustrative character, Nina, standing between an apartment building and a house.

2. **What changes over time.** The view moves from a flat grid of start months, running from January 1991 to July 2016, to a tilted 3D field of houses. It then zooms in to one apartment building and one house with Nina. In frame 2 one tile turns lit, a small amber highlight. In frame 6 a second figure appears next to Nina at the house. The tiles are mostly dark grey in the frames I can see. I can't tell from the image how many ended up lit or dark overall.

3. **What it means.** Whether buying beat renting depends on when you started. Each start month is a separate ten-year trial, and the animation counts how many of those trials favored the buyer. The captions say this is history, not a forecast, and that it covers the US only. Nina is labeled illustrative, so she stands for a hypothetical person, not real data.

4. **Advice a viewer would take.** None. The on-screen text says "Not advice on whether to buy or rent." The animation also doesn't show a result that says which option wins. In the frames I can see, no tally or verdict is given.

5. **Source.** None.
